title: CC-NIC: a Cache-Coherent Interface to the NIC
problem: Emerging cache-coherent interconnects expose NICs to the processor's cache hierarchy, but existing cache coherence abstractions and data structures designed for PCIe are not optimized for host-NIC access patterns, resulting in extraneous communication and cache retention that limits performance.
motivation: Cache-coherent interconnects enable dramatically lower latency and higher performance for NIC operations, requiring interface redesign to fully exploit coherence benefits.
method: CC-NIC redesigns the host-NIC interface specifically for cache-coherent interconnects by rethinking signaling mechanisms and data structure layouts to minimize coherence overheads. The design is modeled using Intel's Ice Lake and Sapphire Rapids UPI interconnects. The approach optimizes access patterns to leverage cache coherence semantics rather than adapting existing PCIe-style interfaces.
key_novelty: Redesigning the host-NIC interface from scratch to optimize for cache coherence semantics rather than applying existing PCIe-based designs to coherent interconnects.
contributions: CC-NIC: a novel host-NIC interface architecture optimized for cache-coherent interconnects
77% lower minimum latency and 88% lower latency at 80% load compared to PCIe NICs
Demonstration of 1.5Gbps packet rate and 980Gbps packet throughput with application-level core savings
Evidence that performance benefits hold across varying interconnect performance characteristics
